verdict.summary: Build one public, multi-user Core API app using OAuth authorization-code flow and Full Dropbox access only if the agent must operate outside its dedicated App Folder. Production distribution is gated by Dropbox approval: Dropbox ordinarily will not review until 50 users have linked the app, although an early-review exception may be available for a compelling detailed case. Least-privilege scopes and a clear user-consent/data-handling explanation are central to approval.
verdict.activeEffort: 4¾–6¾ hours, including secure OAuth/token implementation, testing, and Production-review branding and API-use materials.
verdict.waitTime: A few business days after review begins (official); Dropbox ordinarily will not review until 50 users have linked, and users have two weeks after the 50-user threshold to obtain approval before new linking freezes.
verdict.mainGate: Production readiness approval, ordinarily after 50 linked Dropbox users.

recommendation.text: Register one public Core API app for individual end-user authorization. Select App Folder if the product can genuinely confine all agent work to its dedicated folder; otherwise select Full Dropbox, request only the granular scopes required for the user-enabled workflow, and use progressive authorization for edits or sharing. Do not use the Business API unless the product is explicitly an admin-approved, team-wide offering.

essentials.text: Use authorization-code flow with token_access_type=offline for background agent work. Store the app- and user-specific refresh token encrypted; it is reusable and does not automatically expire, refresh responses do not replace it, and access-token expiry is returned as expires_in. Treat all tokens as opaque secrets that can exceed 1 KB.

sources.quote: you’ll need to include token_access_type=offline as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a refresh_token inside your access token payload.
If this parameter is set to offline , then the access token payload returned by a successful /oauth2/token call will contain a short-lived access_token and a long-lived refresh_token
The refresh token can be repeatedly re-used and doesn't expire automatically (though it can be revoked on demand).
This request won’t return a new refresh token since refresh tokens don’t expire automatically and can be reused repeatedly.
Refresh tokens are app- and user-specific. Developers with multiple app registrations will need to keep track of which app each refresh token is for.
Applications must support variable token size with tokens capable of exceeding 1KB.

steps.title: Configure OAuth callbacks and implement offline code flow

detail.text: In Settings > OAuth 2, register exact HTTPS production and localhost development callback URIs. Implement server-side authorization-code exchange at /oauth2/token, send token_access_type=offline and state to /oauth2/authorize, then encrypt and retain the returned refresh token with its Dropbox user and app association.

steps.output: Scope rationale: The agent requests files.metadata.read to locate user-authorized files. It requests files.content.read only when the user asks it to analyze selected Dropbox content. It requests files.content.write only after the user enables a write action, and sharing.write only when the user explicitly asks to change sharing. The agent processes Dropbox content only to perform the requested feature, records the initiating instruction, and requires explicit confirmation for consequential writes or sharing.

detail.text: With the development app, test a complete system-browser authorization, exact callback and state validation, one-time code exchange, encrypted refresh-token reuse, revoked-token recovery, and API behavior when a required scope is absent. Store token values in variable-length secret fields and send access tokens only as Bearer credentials.

gotchas.text: Do not use a Dropbox OAuth access token as proof of user identity or as an OIDC login substitute; Dropbox states OAuth is authorization, not authentication.

sources.quote: Note: OAuth is an authorization protocol, not an authentication protocol.

gotchas.text: Do not plan to reach the 500-user development cap before applying: after 50 linked users, new linking can freeze if Production approval is not obtained within two weeks.

gotchas.text: Never embed a client_secret in a browser, mobile, or other public client; use authorization-code flow with PKCE where the client cannot protect a secret.

sources.quote: PKCE is an open extension to OAuth 2.0, and solves this problem using dynamic codes instead of the static client_secret .
